nutrients.name: Fiber
notes: The AI is based on 14 g of fiber per 1,000 kcal.
nutrients.summary: The part of plant foods your body cannot digest; it supports regular digestion.

nutrients.name: Sugar
notes: No authoritative daily amount exists for total sugars; the limit applies to added sugars.
nutrients.summary: All sugars in food and drinks, both naturally present and added.

nutrients.name: Added Sugar
notes: Less than 10% of daily calories (Dietary Guidelines 2020-2025).
The Dietary Guidelines 2025-2030 say no amount of added sugars is recommended and that one meal should contain no more than 10 g.
nutrients.summary: Sugars and syrups added to foods and drinks when they are processed or prepared.

nutrients.name: Saturated Fat
notes: Less than 10% of daily calories (both the 2020-2025 and 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines).
nutrients.summary: A type of fat found mostly in meat, full-fat dairy, butter and tropical oils.

nutrients.name: Trans Fat
notes: Keep as low as possible while eating a nutritionally adequate diet; no numeric limit is set.
nutrients.summary: A type of fat found in some processed and fried foods.

nutrients.name: Monounsaturated Fat
notes: No recommended daily amount is set for this fat.
nutrients.summary: A type of fat found in olive oil, avocados and many nuts.

nutrients.name: Polyunsaturated Fat
notes: No recommended daily amount is set for total polyunsaturated fat.
nutrients.summary: A type of fat found in vegetable oils, nuts, seeds and fish; it includes omega-3 and omega-6 fats.

nutrients.name: Omega-3
notes: The AI applies to alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) only; EPA and DHA have no separate recommended amount.
nutrients.summary: Essential fats found in foods such as flaxseed, walnuts and fish.

nutrients.name: Cholesterol
notes: Keep as low as possible while eating a nutritionally adequate diet; no numeric limit is set.
nutrients.summary: A fat-like substance found in animal foods such as eggs, meat and dairy.

nutrients.name: Sodium
notes: 2,300 mg is the Chronic Disease Risk Reduction Intake (CDRR): cutting intake above it is expected to lower chronic disease risk.
The Adequate Intake (AI) for adults is 1,500 mg.
nutrients.summary: A mineral eaten mostly as salt; it helps control the body's fluid balance.

nutrients.name: Potassium
notes: No upper limit is set for potassium from food; people with kidney problems should follow their clinician's advice.
nutrients.summary: A mineral that helps nerves and muscles work and keeps fluid levels normal.

nutrients.name: Calcium
nutrients.summary: A mineral your body needs to build and keep strong bones and teeth.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Iron
notes: People who eat a vegetarian diet need about 1.8 times more iron.
nutrients.summary: A mineral your body uses to make hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Magnesium
nutrients.summary: A mineral involved in muscle and nerve function and in making protein and bone.

upper_limit.note: Applies only to magnesium from supplements and medications, not magnesium in food and drinks.

nutrients.name: Zinc
nutrients.summary: A mineral that helps the immune system and wound healing and is needed to make proteins and DNA.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Phosphorus
nutrients.summary: A mineral that is part of bones, teeth and DNA and of ATP, the molecule cells use to store energy.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Chloride
nutrients.summary: An electrolyte, eaten mostly as salt (sodium chloride), that helps keep the body's fluid balance.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Copper
notes: Amounts are in mg; the RDA of 0.9 mg equals 900 mcg.
nutrients.summary: A mineral that enzymes need for energy production, iron metabolism and making connective tissue.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Manganese
nutrients.summary: A mineral that enzymes need for metabolism, bone formation and protecting cells from damage.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Selenium
notes: In 2023 the European Food Safety Authority set a lower upper limit of 255 mcg a day for adults.
nutrients.summary: A mineral in proteins that support thyroid hormone metabolism, DNA synthesis, reproduction and protection from cell damage.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Chromium
notes: No upper limit is set because no adverse effects have been linked to high intakes from food or supplements.
nutrients.summary: A trace mineral that might help insulin work; how it does so is not yet known.

nutrients.name: Molybdenum
nutrients.summary: A trace mineral that enzymes need to break down sulfur-containing amino acids and other compounds.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Iodine
nutrients.summary: A mineral your thyroid needs to make thyroid hormones.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Vitamin A
notes: Amounts are in mcg retinol activity equivalents (RAE).
nutrients.summary: A vitamin that supports vision, the immune system and reproduction.

upper_limit.note: Applies to preformed vitamin A (retinol and retinyl esters) only; beta-carotene does not count toward it. Ayuvo tracks total vitamin A in mcg RAE, so the line is a guide.

nutrients.name: Vitamin C
notes: People who smoke need 35 mg more vitamin C per day.
nutrients.summary: A vitamin that acts as an antioxidant, helps make collagen and helps absorb iron from plant foods.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Vitamin D
notes: 1 mcg of vitamin D equals 40 IU.
nutrients.summary: A vitamin that helps your body absorb calcium to build and maintain bones.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Vitamin E
notes: Amounts are in mg alpha-tocopherol. 1 IU natural (d-alpha) = 0.67 mg; 1 IU synthetic (dl-alpha) = 0.45 mg.
nutrients.summary: A fat-soluble antioxidant that helps protect cells from damage.

upper_limit.note: Applies to supplemental alpha-tocopherol (supplements and fortified foods), not vitamin E naturally in food.

nutrients.name: Vitamin K
notes: No upper limit is set. People taking blood thinners such as warfarin should keep vitamin K intake steady and follow their clinician's advice.
nutrients.summary: A vitamin needed for normal blood clotting and for bones.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B12
notes: No upper limit is set because of its low potential for toxicity.
nutrients.summary: A vitamin that helps keep nerve and blood cells healthy and helps make DNA.

nutrients.name: Folate
notes: Amounts are in mcg dietary folate equivalents (DFE); 1 mcg DFE = 0.6 mcg folic acid taken with food.
nutrients.summary: A B vitamin needed to make DNA and for cell division.

upper_limit.note: Applies to folic acid from supplements and fortified foods (mcg, not mcg DFE), not folate naturally in food.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B6
notes: In 2023 the European Food Safety Authority set a lower upper limit of 12 mg a day for adults.
nutrients.summary: A B vitamin that enzymes need for protein, carbohydrate and fat metabolism.

upper_limit.note: Applies to food, drinks and supplements combined.

nutrients.name: Thiamin
notes: No upper limit is set because no adverse effects from high intakes from food or supplements have been reported.
nutrients.summary: A B vitamin (vitamin B1) that plays a critical role in turning food into energy.

nutrients.name: Riboflavin
notes: No upper limit is set because no adverse effects from high intakes from food or supplements have been reported.
nutrients.summary: A B vitamin (vitamin B2) that helps produce energy and supports cell growth and function.

nutrients.name: Niacin
notes: Amounts are in mg niacin equivalents (NE); 1 mg NE equals 1 mg niacin or 60 mg of the amino acid tryptophan.
nutrients.summary: A B vitamin (vitamin B3) that the body uses to turn food into energy.

upper_limit.note: Applies only to niacin from supplements and fortified foods (nicotinic acid and nicotinamide), not niacin naturally in food.

nutrients.name: Biotin
notes: No upper limit is set because there is no evidence that biotin is toxic at high intakes.
nutrients.summary: A B vitamin that enzymes need to break down fats, carbohydrates and protein.

nutrients.name: Pantothenic Acid
notes: No upper limit is set because no toxicity from high intakes has been reported.
nutrients.summary: A B vitamin (vitamin B5) that the body uses to make coenzyme A, which it needs to build and break down fats.

nutrients.name: Caffeine
notes: The FDA cites 400 mg a day for most healthy adults as an amount not generally associated with negative effects; sensitivity varies.
nutrients.summary: A stimulant found in coffee, tea, energy drinks and some supplements.

population_note: Values are for adults who are not pregnant or breastfeeding. Under 19, and with no birthday set, Ayuvo uses the 31-50 adult values. Pregnancy and breastfeeding values are not modelled.
